_comment: THE SERVICE AND ENVIRONMENT CATALOG, as a repository declaration.
Program 3 names a 'service/environment catalog' among its nine elements. It
existed as PROSE in the Program 0 release-truth inventory and as frozen JSON
contracts under control-room/contracts/, and as zero rows anywhere. This file
is the declaration; tools/ops-record.py --sync-registry applies it into
ops.service and ops.service_environment. Never hand-edit those tables: the
repo is the source and the database is the render, which is the same posture
every other registry in this system takes.
WHY environment IS 'production' FOR JOBS THAT RUN ON JOE'S MAC. The launchd
jobs are local edge agents by the BDUF's definition, but every one of them
reads and writes the PRODUCTION record layer. The environment field answers
'what was affected', not 'what machine was it typed on' — a Control Room
asking which environment last night's export damaged wants the first answer.
The machine is carried by runtime instead, and for a launchd job by
runs_on: 'primary', 'secondary' or 'every'. lib/launchd_scope.py derives
PRIMARY_ONLY and SECONDARY_ONLY from it, so the installer and this catalog
cannot disagree. sync-registry deliberately does not carry runs_on into
ops.service_environment: placement is installer policy, read from this file.
CADENCE IS WHAT MAKES SILENCE DETECTABLE, so every scheduled service declares
one, and the grace is sized to the real schedule rather than to the ideal:
rules-refresh runs hourly between 07:00 and 20:00, so its true worst-case gap
is the ELEVEN HOURS overnight, and a 3600s cadence would read stale every
morning by design. local-briefs runs weekdays only and its grace spans the
weekend stand-down, the same lesson tools/health-check.py already learned the
expensive way. A cadence that cries wolf nightly is worse than none: it
trains people to stop reading alarms.
A SERVICE WITH NO CADENCE IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT. carr-mcp is not scheduled, so
nothing about it goes stale on a clock; its health comes from synthetic
golden-workflow checks, and until those run it reads unknown — which is the
honest answer for a service nobody has observed.
_comment_scheduled_tasks: THE CLAUDE CODE SCHEDULED TASKS (Program 3, 2026-08-14), registered below
the launchd services. One service per task, keyed IDENTICALLY to the
task's own directory name under ~/.claude/scheduled-tasks/<key>/SKILL.md
(that is also the taskId the scheduler reports and the name the launch
marker in each session's own transcript carries) — no separate mapping
table exists to fall out of sync with either. runtime is
'claude-code-scheduled-task': these are prompts a Claude session executes,
not a script with an exit code, so hooks/scheduled-run-record.py (a Stop
hook) derives the outcome from the session's own transcript
deterministically and records it here — see lib/scheduled_run.py.
nightly-record-layer (above, under the launchd services) already exists as
a service for the launchd chain bin/nightly.sh runs; it is NOT duplicated
here. The Claude session that LAUNCHES that chain is recorded under that
SAME service but the fixed run_key 'scheduled-session' (see
lib/scheduled_run.py RUN_KEY), distinct from the chain's own 'nightly.*'
step keys, so the two can never collide.
ONLY THE CURRENTLY-ENABLED TASKS ARE REGISTERED. x-reply-run-daily,
linkedin-engagement-daily and calendar-fetch-daily are disabled
(`list_scheduled_tasks`, checked 2026-08-14) and deliberately left
unregistered: a cadence-bound service for a task nobody is running would
read STALE forever, which is exactly the false-alarm failure mode
local-briefs' grace design and the launchd services above already learned
to avoid. Register one when its task is re-enabled — sync-registry retires
a service that leaves this file, never the reverse, so nothing is lost by
waiting.
CADENCE for the weekly tasks uses the SAME 604800s/172800s (7 day cadence,
2 day grace) local-briefs already established for a task that can miss its
one weekly window if the Mac is asleep; the monthly tasks (which actually
fire once inside a several-day window via their own internal ledger gate,
per each SKILL.md) use 2592000s/518400s so the window itself is not
mistaken for drift.

services.name: Evening Outlook Inbox triage
services.purpose: Each evening between 19:15 and 21:00, once Joe has been away from the Mac for 10 minutes, restarts the Outlook desktop app into an ordinary window and files already-read Inbox email into Outlook folders by deterministic rules (CARR deal match, A.List vendor, private sender table). Code only: no agent and no model. Unread email is never selected and must still be unread at the end.

environments.notes: Runs on the Mac that holds Joe's Outlook session, today the MacBook (role secondary). Fires every 15 minutes from 19:15 to 21:00 and runs at most once a day: a fire while Joe is active or a draft is open records skipped, and the 21:00 fire settles the day even when skipped, so every day leaves a row by about 21:00 (a success at 19:15 followed by one at 21:00 plus run time the next day is the widest gap, about 27.5 hours). Run rows come from bin/run-scheduled.sh with no names; the moves report stays private in out/outlook-triage/. Installed by bin/install-outlook-triage.sh.

services.name: Outlook mail and calendar intake
services.purpose: Every 30 minutes from 07:00 to 19:00, decodes a private copy of the new Outlook's local store with the pinned hxprobe fork and logs new email (full plain-text body), past meetings and next-seven-day meetings for exactly matched CARR records through log-activity and set-next-action, with one isolated haiku call per new matched email for its next step. Never creates, merges or renames records; never sends anything.

environments.notes: Runs only on the Mac Studio (role primary), using Joe's Main Identity Outlook profile. Fires every 30 minutes from 07:00 to 19:00 local and never overnight, so the record layer can sleep; the 07:00 run catches up from the high-water mark. The grace spans the honest worst case the way rules-refresh's does: the twelve-hour overnight stand-down from 19:00 to 07:00 plus up to 1800s for the succeeded row to leave the local spool. A run whose store is unchanged copies and decodes nothing and makes no record-layer call; its succeeded or skipped row rides the local spool (tools/ops-spool.py) to the next com.carr.run-spool-flush, while a failed row is written directly. Run rows carry counts only; the report, state and needs-refresh list stay private in out/outlook-intake/. Installed by bin/install-outlook-intake.sh.

environments.notes: Primary-only RunAtLoad and a 120-second cadence as StartCalendarInterval (StartInterval never fires on macOS 27), no KeepAlive. ops/tailscale_health.py verifies Running and the kernel route; repair outcomes are timestamped in out/tailscale-up.log.

environments.notes: Grace widened 1800→3600 on 2026-08-18: run rows now ride the local spool (tools/ops-spool.py) and land at the next run-spool-flush, so a row can be inserted up to 1800s after its fire; the old grace put the worst honest gap exactly at the window edge.

services.name: Partner interrupt channel
services.purpose: The Joe/Dell interrupt poll.

environments.notes: Wakes every two minutes, but bin/run-scheduled.sh's --heartbeat-interval (Program 4 follow-up) throttles a SUCCEEDED row to at most one per 1800s — recording all ~720 fires/day as rows would be pure noise from a healthy channel. Every FAILURE is still recorded immediately regardless of the throttle, so cadence here reflects the succeeded heartbeat, not the wake. Grace widened 900→2700 on 2026-08-18: the succeeded row now rides the local spool (tools/ops-spool.py) and is inserted at the next run-spool-flush, up to 1800s after the throttle emitted it, so the honest worst-case gap between inserts is throttle+flush (3600s) against a window of cadence+grace (4500s). Also 2026-08-18: the plist passes --scheduled, which skips the QUERY (never the wake, never the row) outside weekdays 07:00-19:00 local — the last thing keeping the Neon compute from autosuspending. The 2-minute interrupt Joe promised on 2026-08-03 is unchanged during the working day; outside it the job still wakes, still exits 0, and still records its heartbeat through the spool, so this service stays observable overnight exactly as before. This job once logged 382 consecutive identical 'nothing new' lines to a local log with a broken query, because a channel with nothing to say and a channel that cannot ask produce byte-identical output — a run row (even throttled) still distinguishes them, since a genuinely broken query fails loud and goes to the ledger direct, ahead of the spool.

services.name: Capture queue poll
services.purpose: Drains the capture inbox.

environments.notes: Wakes every 5 min, but bin/run-scheduled.sh's --heartbeat-interval (Program 4 follow-up) throttles a SUCCEEDED row to at most one per 1800s (30 min) — recording all ~288 fires/day would be noise from a quiet inbox. Every FAILURE is still recorded immediately regardless of the throttle. Grace widened 900→2700 on 2026-08-18 for the spool delay (tools/ops-spool.py): a succeeded row is inserted at the next run-spool-flush, up to 1800s after it was emitted.

services.name: Calendar EventKit capture
services.purpose: Local, attendee-aware calendar read (EventKit) into stamp-touch, replacing the published feed the Cowork calendar-fetch-daily task read (which Microsoft strips attendees from). Weekdays 07:20. See ops/launchd/com.carr.calendar-eventkit.plist's own header for the PROP-010 ruling this job exists under.

environments.notes: Weekdays at 07:20 only. Grace spans the weekend stand-down (Joe, 2026-07-11), same shape as local-briefs: the real worst-case gap is Friday to Monday, not one day. PR #97 (Program 4 slice 1) wired the other six launchd jobs and deliberately left this one out for lack of a registration; this entry and the plist's own routing through bin/run-scheduled.sh close that gap.

services.name: Run-row spool flusher
services.purpose: The one scheduled door between the local run-row spool (tools/ops-spool.py) and the Neon ledger. Replays queued heartbeat rows through tools/ops-record.py in one batch every 30 minutes, which is what lets the database autosuspend between batches instead of being held awake by a recording every few minutes (2026-08-18 cloud-usage audit).

environments.notes: Criticality HIGH although the job is small: every wrapper-recorded service's freshness now depends on this one draining the queue, so a silently stopped flusher would age every heartbeat at once. Its OWN succeeded row rides the spool it just drained and lands on the NEXT flush — hence a grace wider than its cadence: the steady-state gap between its inserts is one full flush interval plus the next flush's delay. A genuinely failed flush is state=failed and goes to the ledger direct (the spool tries failures direct first), so a broken flusher does not have to wait for itself to be reported.

services.name: Weekly content-fuel harvest
services.purpose: Sources cited market material across the four content lanes and banks it, so the Friday social batch has fuel to draw on.

environments.notes: ENABLED AND UNREGISTERED until 2026-08-15, found by cross-checking list_scheduled_tasks against this file rather than by anything noticing on its own. The registry's own rule above is that only currently-enabled tasks are registered and disabled ones are deliberately left out, so this omission was a gap and not a choice: unregistered it had no cadence, nothing could call it stale, and ops/edge-liveness.py could not see it go quiet from off the Mac. Same 7-day cadence and 2-day grace as every other weekly task, for the reason local-briefs established — a weekly job can miss its one window if the Mac is asleep. Criticality is low because its output feeds the Friday batch rather than any client-facing or recovery path: a missed week costs that batch some fuel and nothing else. Re-registered on the Studio 2026-09-26 after a SECOND registration gap (2026-09-23); verification pending: the first proof run stalled on a tool-approval prompt (session local_7f276c32-2bc0-4484-af4d-08dd24bc5114, still 'running', 36 messages, no readback yet). Cause: an in-progress MacBook->Studio hub move copied this task's SKILL.md onto the Studio (one of 22 folders copied that day) but again never called create_scheduled_task, while the MacBook copy was deleted and its scheduled-tasks.json kept the stale enabled row. Family changed from Local Mac edge to Studio edge: the Studio is the host now, MacBook is a thin client over SSH. This is the same failure class as the 2026-08-15 gap above and neither edge-liveness.py nor any other automated check has caught either occurrence -- both were found by a human cross-check.

services.name: Logitech modifier-key repair
services.purpose: Re-applies the hidutil modifier mapping, which dies on reboot and on receiver replug.

environments.notes: Wakes every 10 min and is idempotent by design, so a missed pass costs a keyboard that behaves oddly until the next one. The cadence is deliberately 2h rather than 10 min, with run-scheduled.sh's heartbeat throttle doing the same job it does for capture-poll: recording 144 identical successes a day would be noise, and a low-criticality cosmetic repair does not earn a row that goes stale within the hour.

services.name: Record-derived egress host allowlist
services.purpose: Regenerates the machine-local host allowlist so the egress guard does not silently fall back to the code list.

environments.notes: NO CADENCE ON PURPOSE, and this one is not a scheduled job that happens to lack a schedule. The plist is SECONDARY MACHINE ONLY: on Joe's primary Mac the allowlist is regenerated as a step of the nightly chain, so this agent is deliberately not installed here and a cadence would report it missing every single day on the one machine where its absence is correct. It is registered so the service EXISTS in the catalog for the machines that do run it.

environments.notes: WatchPaths-triggered, so SILENCE IS THE NORMAL STATE — it fires only when a recording session starts. Any cadence would cry wolf on every day Joe records nothing, which is most days, and an alarm that fires on a quiet day is how both partners learn to stop reading alarms.

services.name: Recording consent announcer

environments.notes: WatchPaths-triggered; silence is normal, so no cadence. Criticality is HIGH despite being a small watcher: it is what makes the rig announce recording aloud, and Florida is an all-party-consent state. A failure here is a legal exposure rather than an inconvenience, which is why it is registered even though nothing can currently observe it firing.

services.name: Cloud nightly backup (GitHub Actions)
services.purpose: The GitHub-hosted Nightly backup (cloud) workflow and its exact failure/disabled/artifact evidence contract; registered so supervised observer-qualified failures can be filed under their true service identity rather than nightly-record-layer.

environments.notes: Externally scheduled by GitHub Actions daily at 02:35 UTC. GitHub native failure email reports a failed run; it does not detect a missed or skipped schedule. GitHub runs are not continuously ingested into ops.run, so expected_cadence_seconds is omitted and CARR service-environment health remains unknown. Missed-run freshness is evaluated separately when the Mac-local nightly-record-layer invokes ops/recovery-point.py on its host-local daily 02:05 schedule. recovery-point.py applies RPO_HOURS=24 to the newest qualified artifact; provider/API unreadability remains unknown. nightly-record-layer's cadence_grace_seconds=7200 is service-health grace, not a guaranteed consumer observation or alert-delivery bound. Observation delay depends on host availability and the timestamp of the last qualified artifact. This is consumer observation, not service cadence ingestion.
